name: Widen a pad without phase smear: high-band pan LFO or hard-panned chord split
goal: Widen a narrow pad without chorus/imager/spreader phase damage using one of two portable methods: (A) multiband-pan only the high band with a slow (bar) or 16th-note sine L/R swirl, keeping lows/mids centered and pulling amount down if motion distracts; or (B) duplicate synth+MIDI, mute alternating chord tones on each copy, and hard-pan L vs R so each side plays different notes of the same harmony—then confirm healthier correlation than chorus.

sources.title: How to widen pads without causing phase issues
How to make true mono compatible stereo widening to your synth sounds #kyaalmix

prerequisites: Pad that sounds good but narrow; for A: multiband pan or band-split + auto-pan; for B: DAW that can duplicate instrument+MIDI and a pad with multi-note chords; correlation/phase meter

inputs.name: lfo_rate
inputs.description: Method A: bar (4/4 slow swirl) or 16th notes; high band only

inputs.name: chord_midi
inputs.description: Method B: pad chord progression to split across two layers

outputs.name: wide_pad
outputs.description: Pad widened by high-band pan motion or by a dual-layer hard-panned complementary chord split

constraints: Ground every step in the source YouTube-provided Show-transcript text; do not invent UI paths or numeric settings not stated there.

Original synthesis / signal-flow only — map brand UI (Ableton/Vital/Serum/VAST/etc.) to portable osc/filter/env/LFO/FX modules for Traveler-inspired or Web Audio hybrid; never rip presets, wavetables, or samples.
Prefer transferable parameter relationships over vendor-specific preset or bank names.
Not affiliated with plugin/synth vendors named in the source videos; recreate with comparable modules.
Prefer these over broadband chorus/imagers when the complaint is phase smear in low/mid.
Method B goal is different L vs R note content—not delayed/frequency-split copies of the same notes.
Delta vs odd/even unison (voice count) and mid/side EQ skills: width here comes from high-band pan modulation or MIDI note splits.

steps.action: Start from a good but narrow pad. Avoid broadband chorus/imager wideners (phasy/warbly, phase issues in lows/mids) and frequency stereo-spread (often not truly wide, can sound inside-out). Choose a method: A) high-band pan LFO on the same patch (steps 2–5), or B) interleaved chord split across two hard-panned layers (steps 6–9).
steps.expect: Pad tone kept; width method chosen

steps.action: Method A: Insert multiband pan / band-limited auto-pan. Solo or target the high band only so lows stay centered.
steps.expect: Only highs are eligible to move L/R

steps.action: Method A: Draw a sine (or subdued sine) pan path so highs slowly swirl L↔R. Try bar-length (4/4) for gentle immersion or 16th-note rate for more motion.
Method A: If 16ths feel too pronounced: switch to a less extreme pan profile and/or lower overall mix/amount of the pan effect.
Method A: A/B before/after in context: pad should envelop more without the washy phase of chorus/imager on full-band signal.
Method B: Duplicate the synth instance with identical settings and copy the MIDI to both tracks.
Method B: On track A piano roll, mute every other note top→bottom; on track B mute the complementary set bottom→top so together they reconstruct the full chords but separately play different notes.
Method B: Hard-pan A fully left and B fully right; play together for maximum width.

Method B: Check a correlation/phase meter: split technique should sit near ~0 (very wide) without deep negative swings; compare vs chorus (often flangy + negative correlation) and spreader (weaker width).
steps.expect: Wide image, healthier correlation than chorus

verification: Only high band is auto-panned; lows remain centered
No full-band chorus/imager on the pad for this width
Mix/amount not so high that motion distracts
Alone, each layer is incomplete chords; together they form full harmony
Hard L/R pan yields strong width
Correlation stays healthier than chorus comparison
